newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas prices extend gains on Southwest heat.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas prices extend gains on Southwest heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices extended their gains Wednesday despite a softer futures market, industry sources said.
Traders blamed the price uptick on a strong cooling demand in the Southwest and storage injections.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices rose three to five cents to the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s, with Transco (Station 65) quoted mostly in the mid-to-high $2.20s.
Ahead of expiry, NYMEX's June Henry Hub futures were down 4.8 cents at $2.315 at 1402 EDT, mirroring early Gulf cash prices for June 1 in the low-$2.30s.
Temperatures in the Southwest, including southern California were expected to reach highs in the 90s and 100 degrees plus, Weather Services Corp reported.
As a result, southern California border prices gained another six cents to the low-to-mid $2.20s. Permian prices were also higher at $2.06-$2.14.
However, some power is expected to return to the electricity grid later today, which should relieve the tight supply situation, traders said.

The 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit, shut late Monday for repairs, is expected to restart Wednesday night, while Texas Utilities' 1,150 MW Comanche Peak 2 unit is also expected to return to full power later today.

But Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit will not restart until this weekend, the company said earlier today. The unit was originally expected to exit its refueling outage Thursday.

For June 1 delivery, Permian prices were quoted around $2.10, while the San Juan market hovered around $2.05-$2.06, traders said, adding that southern California border prices were talked in the low-$2.20s.
In south Texas, hot weather and humidity pushed prices three cents higher into the low-$2.20s. Temperatures in Houston are forecast to reach highs in the high-80s through Friday.
In the Midwest, prices for Thursday rose another three cents to about $2.12-$2.14, while June 1 values were talked mostly at $2.15.
Temperatures in Chicago were forecast to reach highs in the low-60s Thursday and Friday, WSC said.
In the East, New York city gate prices were quoted at $2.48-$2.50.
